test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In gasoline direct injection, which type of control adjusts the air-fuel ratio in real time based on oxygen sensor data?
solution:
The correct answer is __Closed-loop control**(Option 2)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Closed-loop control__ is an automatic control system.
 
• It adjusts the air-fuel ratio in real time based on oxygen sensor feedback.
 
• This ensures optimal combustion efficiency and minimizes emissions.
 
• Closed-loop systems continuously monitor output parameters to achieve desired results.
 
• It contrasts with open-loop systems that do not use feedback for adjustments.
 
• The oxygen sensor plays a critical role in detecting the exhaust's oxygen content to regulate the air-fuel mixture.
 
• Such systems are widely used in modern gasoline direct injection engines.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Open-loop control:**

 
 
• Operates without feedback, relying solely on preset instructions.
 
• Less accurate as it cannot adapt to changes in system conditions.
 
 
 
• **Feed-forward control:**
 
 
• Anticipates disturbances and adjusts inputs accordingly.
 
• Does not rely on feedback for real-time adjustments.
 
 
 
• **Indirect control:**
 
 
• Manages system variables indirectly through intermediate parameters.
 
• Less commonly used in engine control systems.
